\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{どこ} (doko)}{どこ (doko)}]{\ja{どこ} (doko) — where}

\label{lesson:JA-C78-doko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for the fifth of the month; some day, then the Japanese for the sixth of the month.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{どこ}}
\textbf{\ja{どこ}} — \emph{doko} — \textquotedblleft{}where\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{どこ}} (\emph{doko}) is native: \emph{do-}, the root of \textquotedblleft{}which\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-ko}, \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{}, as in \emph{koko}, \textquotedblleft{}here\textquotedblright{}. It is inherited rather than borrowed, and JMdict marks it as usually written in kana.
\end{cousinweb}
